[[Chartered Accountant]]
[[London Business School]] ([[MBA]]) | occupation = | title = [[Chairman]] of [[Aditya Birla Group]] | spouse = {{marriage| Neerja Birla |1989}} | children = 3 (including [[Ananya Birla|Ananya]]) | parents = [[Aditya Vikram Birla]] and [[Rajashree Birla]] | awards = [[Padma Bhushan]] (2023) | relatives = See [[Birla family]] }} '''Kumar Mangalam Birla''' (born 14 June 1967) is an Indian billionaire businessman. He is the chairman of the [[Aditya Birla Group]], one of the largest [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerates]] in India. He is the chancellor of the [[Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani]]{{cite web |title=Mr. Kumar Mangalam Birla – Chairman of the Aditya Birla Group |url=http://www.adityabirla.com/the_group/km_birla_profile.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121110201120/http://www.adityabirla.com/the_group/km_birla_profile.htm |archive-date=10 November 2012 |access-date=27 December 2016}} and former chairman of [[Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad]].{{cite news |date=23 October 2016 |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla appointed as new chairman of IIM-A |url=http://indianexpress.com/article/education/kumar-mangalam-birla-appointed-as-new-chairman-of-iim-a-3097993/ |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]]}} In 2023, Birla received the [[Padma Bhushan]], the third highest civilian honour in India.{{Cite news |date=2023-03-22 |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla receives Padma Bhushan award |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/kumar-mangalam-birla-receives-padma-bhushan-award/article66650520.ece |access-date=2024-11-19 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} As of August 2026, ''[[Forbes]]'' estimated his net worth at US$24 billion.{{cite web |title=Forbes Profile: Kumar Birla |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/kumar-birla/ |access-date=9 December 2024 |website=Forbes.com}} Born to [[Aditya Vikram Birla]], the eldest of two children, he took over as chairman of the Aditya Birla Group in 1995, at the age of 28, following the death of his father.{{cite news |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla History Maker Founder of Aditya Birla Group |url=https://www.indiaherald.com/Politics/Read/342384/Kumar-Mangalam-Birla-History-Maker-Founder-of-Aditya-Birla-Group |work=APHerald [Andhra Pradesh Herald] |language=en}}{{Cite news |title=I had no choice but to grow up fast: Kumar Mangalam Birla |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/anniversary/story/20210104-i-had-no-choice-but-to-grow-up-fast-1753013-2020-12-26}} During Birla's tenure as chairman, the group's annual turnover increased from US$2 billion in 1995 to US$70 billion as of August 2026,{{cite web |date=24 January 2013 |title=Aditya Birla Group: Of challenges and opportunities |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/aditya-birla-group-of-challenges-and-opportunities-112090900061_1.html |access-date=25 July 2022 |website=Business Standard}} with operations in 40 countries.{{Cite web |date=2024-08-12 |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla |url=https://gulfbusiness.com/lists/most-influential-indians-in-the-region-2024/kumar-mangalam-birla/ |access-date=2024-11-19 |language=en-US}} ==Early life and education== A fourth generation member of the [[Birla Family]] from Pilani, Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, Birla was born in Kolkata and grew up in a joint family in Mumbai with his parents [[Aditya Vikram Birla]] and [[Rajashree Birla]] and younger sister Vasavadatta Birla.{{cite web |title=Forbes Profile: Kumar Birla |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/kumar-birla/ |access-date=25 March 2023 |website=Forbes.com}}{{cite web |title=The story of the first couple of the Birla empire |url=https://www.rediff.com/money/slide-show/slide-show-1-the-story-of-the-first-couple-of-the-birla-empire/20110706.htm |access-date=6 February 2019 |website=Rediff.com}} He is the descendent of the adopted son (Baldeo Das Birla) of wealthy opium trader Shiv Narayan Birla in the late 19th century. He did his high school from [[Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics]] and a bachelor's degree from [[H.R. College of Commerce and Economics]] of the [[University of Mumbai]]. He later studied at [[London Business School]] and obtained [[Master of Business Administration]] from [[University of London]] in 1992. He is also an honorary fellow at LBS. He is a [[chartered accountant]] from [[Institute of Chartered Accountants of India]] (ICAI).{{Cite web |title=Mr. Kumar Mangalam Birla |url=https://www.adityabirla.com/about-us/leadership/kumar-mangalam-birla |website=abg.com}} === Family and children === In January 2023, Birla's children, [[Ananya Birla]] and [[Aryaman Birla|Aryaman Vikram Birla]], were appointed as Directors of [[Grasim Industries]], [[Hindalco Industries]], and Aditya Birla Management Corporation Private Limited (ABMCPL), and joined the board of [[Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail|Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited]] (ABFRL).{{Cite web |title=Aditya Birla Group Chairman Kumar Mangalam's children Ananya, Aryaman join Hindalco board |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/aditya-birla-group-chairman-kumar-mangalam-birlas-children-inducted-on-board-of-hindalco-11723603214890.html |website=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]|date=14 August 2024 |author1=Shivangini }} ==Career== === 1995–2015 === In 1995, Birla took over the family business and consolidated all the group companies under the brand – Aditya Birla Group (ABG).{{cite web|url=https://www.rediff.com/money/2005/sep/19spec.htm|title=Kumar Mangalam: The biggest Birla|website=Rediff|date=19 September 2005|access-date=1 March 2022}} Birla acquired [[Hindalco Industries|Indian Aluminum Company]] (INDAL) in 2000.{{Cite web |title=Milestones – Aditya Birla Group |url=https://www.adityabirla.com/about-us/milestones |access-date=2022-12-05 |website=abg.com |language=en}} In 2003, Hindalco Industries acquired Nifty Copper Mines in Australia, while the Aditya Birla Group acquired the Mount Gordon Copper mines in Australia.{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/hindalco-to-acquire-nifty-copper-mine-in-australia/articleshow/35377714.cms|title=Hindalco to acquire Nifty copper mine in Australia|website=The Times of India|date=24 January 2003|access-date=1 March 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/birla-copper-buys-aussie-mining-firm/71399/|title=Birla Copper Buys Aussie Mining Firm|website=Financial Express|date=25 January 2003|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2004, Birla acquired a majority stake in L&T Cement, which was later renamed UltraTech Cement.{{cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/todays-paper/tp-corporate/article28886849.ece|title= L&T Cement is now UltraTech Cement|website=The Hindu Businessline|date=14 October 2004|access-date=1 March 2022}} In the same year, Hindalco Industries announced a merger with all the businesses of Indian Aluminium Company (Indal).{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/business-empires-the-birlas/av-birla-group/indal/indals-metals-businesses-to-be-merged-with-hindalco/articleshow/907010.cms? |title= Indal's metals businesses to be merged with Hindalco|website=The Economic Times|date=24 August 2004|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2007, Hindalco acquired Atlanta-based Novelis Inc, which was the world's leading producer of aluminium rolled products.{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/india/hindalco-buys-us-based-novelis-inc-for-6-billion/story-ewOSGIxUarxJKacMDITWEL.html|title= Hindalco buys US-based Novelis Inc for $6 billion|website=Hindustan Times|date=17 February 2007|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2012, Birla's Aditya Birla Nuvo Ltd acquired Future Group's Pantaloon Retail Limited in India.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/7gYxcYC8xH8OjggQWmIfAJ/Aditya-Birla-to-buy-Pantaloons-retail-chain.html |title= Aditya Birla to buy Pantaloons retail chain |website=Livemint|date=1 May 2012|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2013, Aditya Birla Chemicals acquired the chlor-alkali and phosphoric acid divisions of Solaris Chemtech Industries in India.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Home-Page/B2xairAeMOhSwU3Xi1tzGN/Aditya-Birla-Chem-to-acquire-Solaris-Chemtech-unit.html|title= Aditya Birla Chem to acquire Solaris Chemtech unit|website=Livemint|date=31 May 2013|access-date=1 March 2022}} Birla's name surfaced in [[Indian coal allocation scam|Indian coal allocation scandal]], pertaining to the allocation of coal blocks between 2004 and 2009.{{cite web |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla embroiled in Coalgate case with CBI filing 14th FIR |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/kumar-mangalam-birla-embroiled-in-coalgate-case-with-cbi-filing-14th-fir/1183040/ |website=financialexpress.com |date=16 October 2013}} In 2014, CBI filed closure report against Birla.{{cite web |title=CBI files closure report against Kumar Mangalam Birla in coal block allocation scam |url=https://m.businesstoday.in/story/cbi-closure-report-against-kumar-mangalam-birla-coal-scam/1/209815.html |website=m.businesstoday.in |date=29 August 2014 |language=en}} Since 2015, the Aditya Birla Group consolidated its branded apparel business under its lifestyle retail firm Pantaloons Fashion and Retail India Ltd and renamed it as Aditya Birla Fashion & Retail, creating India's largest branded clothing company by revenue and number of sales outlets.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/Tkmkh24tHNUfX21ngDTgTP/Aditya-Birla-Group-to-merge-Madura-Garments-with-Pantaloon-R.htm|title=Aditya Birla Group to merge apparel business units|website=Livemint|date=4 May 2015|access-date=1 March 2022}}{{Dead link|date=May 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} === 2016–present === By 2016, Birla launched a new logo for the [[Aditya Birla Group]].{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/aditya-birla-group-logo-gets-a-young-makeover/articleshow/54258423.cms|title=Aditya Birla Group logo gets a young makeover|website=The Times of India|date=10 September 2016|access-date=1 March 2022}} In June 2017, [[UltraTech Cement]], chaired by Birla, completed the acquisition of Jaiprakash Associates' six cement plants along with five grinding units.{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/cement/ultratech-completes-acquisition-of-jaiprakash-group-cement-business/articleshow/59372842.cms?from=mdr |title=UltraTech completes acquisition of Jaiprakash group cement business |website=The Times of India|date=29 June 2017|access-date=1 March 2022}} In the same year, Birla revived [[Applause Entertainment]], a media, content and IP creation studio with a focus on creating premium digital drama series.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/gcAeHpIUwsSH0mfx612uUM/Kumar-Mangalam-Birla-revives-Applause-Entertainment-for-cont.html|title=Kumar Mangalam Birla revives Applause Entertainment for content play|website=Livemint|date=17 August 2017|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2018, the Aditya Birla Group-owned [[Idea Cellular]] merged with [[Vodafone India]] to create India's then largest telecom service provider, [[Vodafone Idea]]. Also in 2018, UltraTech Cement acquired the cement business of Century Textiles, while [[Binani Cement]] became a wholly owned subsidiary of UltraTech Cement.{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/ultratech-to-buy-centurys-cement-biz-in-rs-8621cr-deal/articleshow/64249959.cms|title=UltraTech to buy Century's cement business in Rs 8,621 crore deal|website=The Times of India|date=21 May 2018|access-date=1 March 2022}} {{cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/binani-cement-becomes-ultratechs-subsidiary/article25559146.ece|title=Binani Cement becomes UltraTech's subsidiary|website=The Hindu Businessline|date=21 November 2018|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2018, Novelis entered into an agreement to acquire Aleris Corporation. The deal was closed for $2.8 billion in 2020.{{cite web|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/hindalco-s-subsidiary-novelis-completes-2-8-bn-acquisition-of-aleris-120041401583_1.html |title=Hindalco's subsidiary Novelis completes $2.8 bn acquisition of Aleris |website=Business Standard|date=14 April 2020|access-date=1 March 2022}} In 2021, Grasim Industries entered the paints business with an investment of {{INR}}₹10,000 crore, paid over three years.{{cite web | last=Maloo | first=Mangalam | title=Grasim Paints Launch: Profitability, ₹10,000 crore revenue in three years, says Kumar Mangalam Birla | website=CNBCTV18 | date=2024-02-22 | url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/grasim-share-price-paints-business-launch-profitable-10000-crore-revenue-in-three-years-km-birla-units-dealers-19109361.htm | access-date=2025-03-24}}{{cite web |date=28 August 2021 |title=Grasim approves Rs 5,000-crore capex for paints business |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/paper-/-wood-/-glass/-plastic/-marbles/grasim-approves-rs-5000-crore-capex-for-paints-business/articleshow/85688010.cms? |access-date=1 March 2022 |website=Economic Times}} In August 2021, Birla stepped down as the non-executive chairman of Vodafone Idea.{{cite web |date=5 August 2021 |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla steps down from Vodafone Idea board after stake offer |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/kumar-mangalam-birla-steps-down-from-vodafone-idea-board-after-stake-offer-121080500040_1.html |access-date=1 March 2022 |website=Business Standard}}{{cite web |date=24 September 2018 |title=Kumar Mangalam Birla: As acquisitive as ever |url=https://www.fortuneindia.com/enterprise/kumar-mangalam-birla-as-acquisitive-as-ever/102494 |access-date=1 March 2022 |website=Fortune India}} [[File:Kumar Mangalam Birla at ET Business Leader of the Year Award.jpg|thumb|right|Birla receiving the ET Business Leader of the Year Award from Finance Minister [[Nirmala Sitharaman]]]] Under Birla's chairmanship, [[UltraTech Cement]] announced plans to expand its grey cement production capacity to 200 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) with an investment of ₹32,400 crore.{{Cite web |last=Suri |first=Naman |title=UltraTech announces ₹32,400 crore capex for expansion in the next three years |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/ultratech-announces-32-400-crore-capex-for-expansion-in-the-next-three-years-11712071622084.html |website=[[Mint (newspaper)|Mint]]}} In November 2023, he oversaw the acquisition of [[Kesoram Industries]]' cement assets for ₹7,600 crore.{{Cite news |date=2023-12-01 |title=UltraTech to buy building materials business of Kesoram in 7,600 crore deal |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/ultratech-to-buy-building-materials-business-of-kesoram-in-7600-crore-deal/articleshow/105638805.cms |access-date=2024-11-19 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}} By the end of 2023, UltraTech had increased its production capacity by 18.7 MTPA, with an additional 35.5 MTPA in a planned manner across 16 locations. In April 2024, two new greenfield projects were commissioned, adding 5.4 MTPA in [[Chhattisgarh]] and [[Tamil Nadu]].{{Cite news |date=2024-04-02 |title=UltraTech Cement crosses 150 mtpa capacity milestone |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/ultratech-cement-crosses-150-mtpa-capacity-milestone/article68020958.ece |access-date=2024-11-19 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} By April 2024, UltraTech's total grey cement manufacturing capacity had reached 151.6 MTPA. In July 2024, Aditya Birla Group launched its jewellery brand Indriya with an investment of {{INR}}5,000 crore.{{Cite news |last=Bhattacharyya |first=Rica |date=2024-11-05 |title=Novel Jewels to open 100 stores in 18 months |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/fashion-/-cosmetics-/-jewellery/novel-jewels-to-open-100-stores-in-18-months/articleshow/114956682.cms?from=mdr Kumar Mangalam Birla (born 14 June 1967) is an Indian billionaire businessman. He is the chairman of the Aditya Birla Group, one of the largest conglomerates in India. He is the chancellor of the Birla Institute of Technology & Science, Pilani and former chairman of Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad. In 2023, Birla received the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian honour in India.
As of August 2026, Forbes estimated his net worth at US$24 billion.
Born to Aditya Vikram Birla, the eldest of two children, he took over as chairman of the Aditya Birla Group in 1995, at the age of 28, following the death of his father. During Birla's tenure as chairman, the group's annual turnover increased from US$2 billion in 1995 to US$70 billion as of August 2026, with operations in 40 countries.
